exercise1.prompt: Reading JSON Data: Columns from records

hiddenCases.name: a key only some records have still becomes a column
pandas builds the table
hiddenCases.describe: a DataFrame built from the records

exercise1.hint: pd.DataFrame takes the list of dictionaries directly. sorted(df.columns) then gives plain strings in a predictable order.

exercise2.prompt: Reading JSON Data: How complete is each record

hiddenCases.name: a fully populated table counts every row
an explicit None counts as missing

exercise2.hint: df.notna().sum() gives a Series of counts per column. Turn it into a dict and make the values plain ints with a comprehension.

choices: One row per dictionary, keys as columns
questions.explain: A list of records is a table waiting to happen; the union of the keys becomes the columns.

questions.prompt: A record is missing a key the others have. What goes in that cell?
questions.explain: The column exists because other records have it, and this row simply has no value for it.

questions.prompt: A value is itself a dictionary. What does DataFrame give you?
questions.explain: json_normalize is what flattens one level into real columns, named with a dot.

questions.prompt: Whole-number scores with one record missing the key get which dtype?
questions.explain: NaN is a float, so the column widens to hold it — the same rule as anywhere else in pandas.
